I fetched the page and the quoted words are on it, word for word. This candidate is the same claim as one already on file, so the admission is "recorded".

**Page check.** The page is Tom Rochette's blog. In his own words it "contains most of the content of the slides" of a Demis Hassabis talk, and it links to the talk's YouTube recording (IjG_Fx3D0o0). Under the heading "Predictions" there is a bullet that reads: "Probably ~20+ years for full human-level AGI but lots of interesting technologies will be built on the way." That matches the quote exactly. This is a third party's typed-up copy of the slides, not Hassabis's own post, a transcript or a printed Q&A, so on its own it counts as coverage only. The YouTube recording it links to could serve as the primary source, but I did not open it.

**Date.** The page gives no date for the talk and does not name the FHI Winter Intelligence Conference. The only dates on it are the blog's own: created 2016-03-18 and updated 2026-04-08. The search run's date of 2011-01-16, and its description of the occasion, come from somewhere other than this page.

**The four parts of the rule:**
1. **Role.** DeepMind was co-founded in 2010, so in January 2011 Hassabis was its co-founder and chief executive. Whether the small DeepMind of 2011 already counted as "a company that builds frontier AI models" is debatable. The ledger has already admitted two 2011 claims from him, so it has evidently accepted the role.
2. **About AI and forward-looking.** Yes. It is a timing forecast for "full human-level AGI". Under ruled reading 4, bare "human level" is an undefined stage, so it will probably carry no testable bar. That affects how the claim is scored, not whether it is admitted.
3. **Date or span.** "~20+ years" is a span counted from the day it was said. Because of the "+", it reads more like "at least twenty years" than "by twenty years".
4. **Source.** Only coverage is confirmed. The recording would need checking to upgrade it to a primary source.

**Already recorded.** The person's claim files include `2011-01-hassabis-human-level-agi-twenty-plus-years.toml`, which has the same speaker, occasion, words and span. Under the Restatements rule this is the same claim, not a new one, so it should not be entered again.
